text: We have a big breaking news coming in from the Middle East where the war has exploded yet again.
Iran has launched a ballistic missile attack targeting U.S. military facilities in the region,
marking yet another major escalation in tensions between Tehran and Washington.
This comes after four days of peace. For four days, we saw no attacks from Tehran or Washington.
But now, according to Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps or the IRGC,
its aerospace force fired ballistic missiles at U.S. airbase and a U.S. Central Command facility in Jordan.
Iranian state-affiliated media says the attack was carried out in response to recent American military actions against Iran.
However, the United States is presenting a different picture.
U.S. Central Command says Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles in what it called an attempted surprise attack
against American forces in the Middle East.
Why this is a surprise?
Because America and Iran were back on the table negotiating peace, negotiating the nuclear program.
According to CENTCOM, all incoming missiles were successfully intercepted and no damage or casualties have been reported so far.
Meanwhile, CNN, citing a U.S. official, reports that early intelligence assessments indicate Iran may have launched fewer than four ballistic missiles,
suggesting the attack may have been more limited than initially feared.
But the military exchanges did not stop viewers.
In a significant counter-operation, United States and Saudi Arabian forces carried out precision airstrikes,
sort of a joint operation inside Iraq, targeting logistic hubs and weapons sites allegedly used by Iran-aligned armed groups,
the proxy groups.
CENTCOM says these strikes were conducted after more than 30 drone attacks over the past 72 hours,
targeting U.S. personal and Saudi energy infrastructure.
The U.S. military also claims that between February and April this year,
there were more than 600 attempted attacks on American citizens and facilities by Iran-backed militias operating inside Iraq.
So now the message from Washington is clear.
The United States says Iran and its allied groups must halt these attacks or face further military action.
At this stage, there are conflicting claims over the scale of Iran's missile launch.
But both Iranian and U.S. officials have confirmed that missiles were fired toward American positions,
making this one of the most serious direct confrontation this week.
The situation remains extremely fluid with risk of further escalation across the Middle East.
Now that Saudi Arabia has entered the picture directly,
we will continue to track every development and bring you updates as they come in.
Stay with us for more on this.
